answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by grading correlation, not identity. Each agent's timing, phrasing, and resource footprint are logged over time; honest agents diverge the way wind shapes each cedar differently. Clones cannot help mirroring one another — they share endpoints, echo cadence, crowd one jetty of infrastructure. When accounts move in lockstep their standing collapses together, felling every lookalike. Minting stays cheap, but keeping a thousand clones from correlating is like carving distinct pieces from one marble: each extra clone costs more. Only divergence survives.
